overview: Goryeo unified the Korean peninsula and oversaw a golden age of Buddhist culture and artistic achievement. The dynasty is famous for its exquisite celadon ceramics, the Tripitaka Koreana woodblocks and pioneering metal movable type printing.

items.text: World's first metal movable type printing developed, which predated Gutenberg by two centuries.
Tripitaka Koreana carved on 81,352 wooden blocks, the most complete Buddhist canon.
Celadon ceramics with jade-green glaze and inlaid designs reach perfection.
Buddhist paintings, sculptures and illuminated manuscripts produced.
The Tripitaka Koreana woodblocks remain at Haeinsa Temple, still usable after 800 years.
Buddhism received extensive state patronage, with temples and monasteries flourishing.
Civil service examinations based on Chinese classics and Buddhist texts.
The name Korea derives from Goryeo, reflecting its historical importance.
Celadon ceramics and Tripitaka Koreana remain national treasures.

fall.text: General Yi Seong-gye overthrew the last Goryeo king and established the Joseon dynasty in 1392.
